actions.reason: The RNA report describes a coherent, candidate-specific metabolic phenotype (coordinated OXPHOS/mitochondrial down-regulation, NES -1.97, FDR 0.001, with shared leading-edge genes indicating one axis). The set-level confounder report shows no significant technical, site, or acquisition association with membership after correction, so the measured factors do not provide a substantial alternative explanation. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable within-set cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision signal, and the nearest-pair affinities are only modestly close. The candidate has an interpretable identity and no material unresolved alternative explanation; the heterogeneous-rest and small-size limitations are acknowledged but do not undermine independent retention.

The RNA report describes a strong, coherent immune-down/metabolic-up phenotype (allograft rejection NES -2.72, interferon gamma -2.63, OXPHOS +2.56, all FDR 0.001), and the WXS report adds a complementary, multiplicity-robust VHL depletion (0/15 vs 56/88, q_global 0.0066) that distinguishes this set from the VHL-mutant majority. The set-level confounder report is uniformly null, so measured technical factors do not provide a substantial alternative explanation. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision. The TP53 enrichment is panel-level only and the rest group is heterogeneous, but the integrated evidence positively supports an interpretable identity and independent retention.

The RNA report describes an interpretable inflammatory-up phenotype, but the candidate-specific cross-modal report shows the current boundary is essentially unseparated in RNA (silhouette 0.0016) and WSI (-0.0399), only weakly separated in CT (0.0203), and modestly separated in WXS (0.0880), with within- and between-label distances nearly identical in CT and RNA and reversed in WSI. The set-level confounder report shows strong, corrected associations with tissue source site (Cramér's V 0.490, q=0.003), CT scanner model (0.433, q=0.016), and CT slice thickness/z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.185/0.188, q=4.1e-05), leaving a material site/acquisition alternative explanation for the set-versus-rest contrast. The WXS report shows no robust driver-panel signature, only a single non-driver FLG enrichment. The requested cross-modal evidence was acquired and does not resolve the boundary weakness; the full evidence does not positively justify treating this membership as an independent candidate unit.

The RNA report describes a very broad down-regulation across immune, EMT, cell-cycle, and metabolic programs, but the breadth and shared leading-edge genes indicate a single global axis rather than a specific candidate identity, and the WXS report is essentially null at the driver-panel level with only nominal uncorrected non-driver enrichments. The set-level confounder report is nonsignificant, so technical factors are not the dominant concern; the weakness is that the evidence does not positively establish a defensible independent identity or boundary for this membership. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision. The candidate has not earned independent retention, though its observed biology may be real.

The RNA report describes a strong, coherent immune-up phenotype (interferon gamma NES 2.87, allograft rejection 2.84, interferon alpha 2.83, all FDR 0.001), and the WXS report adds a robust, globally significant BAP1 enrichment (11/20 vs 2/83, q_global 0.000195), the strongest driver signal among the sets. The set-level confounder report is nonsignificant after correction, so measured technical factors do not provide a substantial alternative explanation. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision. The BAP1/immune-up alignment is biologically interpretable, and the integrated evidence positively supports independent retention.

The RNA report describes a broad metabolic/proliferative down-regulation, but the candidate-specific cross-modal report shows the current boundary is aligned only with CT (silhouette 0.108) and is essentially unseparated in RNA (0.0015) and slightly negative in WSI (-0.0232) and WXS (-0.0148), with between-label distances smaller than or equal to within-label distances in those views. The WXS report shows no robust driver-panel signature, only a single non-driver ATM enrichment, and the set is the smallest (8 samples), substantially limiting stability. The set-level confounder report is null, so technical factors are not the concern; the concern is that the requested cross-modal evidence does not establish a defensible independent boundary. The full evidence does not positively justify independent retention.

The RNA report describes a coherent, candidate-specific ECM/EMT-up phenotype (EMT NES 2.53, FDR 0.001, with shared collagen/matrix leading-edge genes) together with OXPHOS down-regulation, which is a distinct program relative to the other sets. The set-level confounder report is nonsignificant after correction, so measured technical factors do not provide a substantial alternative explanation. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision. The candidate has an interpretable identity and no material unresolved alternative explanation; the heterogeneous-rest and small-size limitations are acknowledged but do not undermine independent retention.

The RNA report describes a proliferation-up/immune-down phenotype, but the candidate-specific cross-modal report shows the current boundary is aligned only with WSI (silhouette 0.120) and is negative in CT (-0.0402), near zero in RNA (-0.0023), and only weakly positive in WXS (0.0318), with between-label distances smaller than within-label in CT and RNA. The WXS report shows only a panel-level PBRM1 enrichment that does not survive global correction, and the set is the smallest (7 samples), substantially limiting stability. The set-level confounder report is weak and nonsignificant, so technical factors are not the concern; the concern is that the requested cross-modal evidence does not establish a defensible independent boundary. The full evidence does not positively justify independent retention.
